newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sakakibara says no comment on BOJ rate check talk.
newsitem.headline: Sakakibara says no comment on BOJ rate check talk.

text.p: Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the International Finance Bureau at the Ministry of Finance, told Reuters on Tuesday he could not comment on market rumours that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) had conducted rate checks on the dollar/yen rate at around 120 yen.
Asked about market rumours that the BOJ called commercial banks when the dollar rose to 120 yen in a bid to check the dollar's further rise, Sakakibara said: "I cannot comment on that."
He also declined to comment on the current dollar/yen levels.
The dollar rose to a high of 120.05 yen by mid-afternoon Tokyo trading, compared with its New York close of 119.55/60 yen on Monday.
Some dealers were sceptical about the rate check rumours, noting the presence of fairly large offers at 120 yen and above that made the dollar top-heavy.
A trader at a major city bank said there were rumours the BOJ was checking rates, but that actually there were no phone calls made beyond the regular calls requesting information.
